declarations.name: beekem_theorem1_imported_normalized
declarations.location: Section 5, Theorem 1, page 10; proof in Appendix B, pages 17-19
declarations.exact_game: BeeKemKiGame over the executable Figure 8 oracle environment, with bee_safe_kappa computed by the challenger from the complete accepted/rejected query log
declarations.quantifier_order: For every KI adversary A, every single concrete BeeKEM[SE,NIKE] PaperInstance, and every game parameter tuple satisfying the side conditions, there exist BNike and BSe before the reduction bound.
declarations.witness_dependency: Because BNike and BSe are existentially quantified inside the conclusion after universal A and PaperInstance, they may depend on the challenged adversary, the exact paper instance, and the public game parameters. They are not unrelated universally quantified primitive adversaries.
primitive_reductions: BNike is an existential Appendix-B witness run in BeeKemHkrCksGame(BNike, BeeKemNikeOfPaperInstance(PaperInstance), BeeKemNikeSamplerOfPaperInstance(PaperInstance))
BSe is an existential Appendix-B witness run in BeeKemMuCpaGame(BSe, BeeKemSeOfPaperInstance(PaperInstance))
declarations.query_bounds: The executable KI game evidence satisfies bke_challenge_count <= c and bke_member_addition_count <= n with probability 1.
declarations.reduction_loss: beekem_theorem1_loss c h = c * h, under the executable relation beekem_is_ceil_log2 n h characterizing h = ceil(log2 n)
side_conditions: the exact NIKE adapter is symmetric/correct with probability 1
the exact symmetric-encryption adapter is correct for every message with probability 1
the executable game-derived challenge and member-addition counts obey c and n
declarations.correctness_specialization: The imported boundary uses perfect NIKE symmetry and perfect symmetric-encryption correctness. This is a narrower specialization than the paper's overwhelming-correctness formulation; it does not silently turn correctness failure into zero.
declarations.query_log_semantics: Every state-transition or safety-relevant create, add, remove, update, deliver, reveal, challenge, and compromise attempt is appended with bq_accepted and an optional rejection reason. Figure 8's perpetual read-only access to the control/direct message maps is modeled as a direct read and is not counted as a safety query. Safety, reveal history, compromise history, challenge counts, and member-addition counts use successful game events rather than adversary-supplied admissibility flags.
declarations.q2op_interpretation: A successful operation-bearing query maps to its recorded operation. A successful snapshot compromise maps conservatively to the actor's challenger-maintained causal frontier at that query. Rejected queries and successful queries without an operation/frontier contribution map to the empty set.
threat_model_boundary: honest BeeKEM execution by protocol participants
adversarial scheduling and network partitions within ACB
adaptive reveal, challenge, and snapshot-compromise queries
finite kappa >= 1 with explicit retained-personal-secret behavior
no arbitrary Byzantine deviation by a genuinely authorized member
no application authorization, live-key, history-key, or Rust implementation theorem
declarations.normalization: Uniform centered bias abs(Pr[guess = bit] - 1/2) is used for KI-DCGKA, HKR-CKS, and MU-CPA. Page 10 prints raw success probability, while Appendix B uses absolute neighboring-game probability differences. Applying the same factor-two convention to every game leaves the stated reduction factors unchanged.
declarations.machine_check_status: The typed protocol state, Figure 8/9 oracle environment, complete query log, finite-kappa safety predicate, hidden-bit KI game, c/n counters, named primitive games, side-condition games, theorem quantifier shape, and mutation witnesses are EasyCrypt-checked. The Appendix-B reduction proof and the internal algorithms of the existential witnesses BNike/BSe are the sole imported paper evidence.

beekem_checker_evidence.evidence_note: This committed manifest names the immediately preceding checker-accepted proof and CI-guard baseline. The documentation commit containing this record necessarily has a later workflow run and cannot self-reference its own artifact digest.

mutation_results.theorem_boundary: Deleting the existential BNike witness made the audit exit 1; CI accepted only that expected rejection.
mutation_results.dependency_closure: Deleting BeeKemSafety.ec made the EasyCrypt compile exit 1; CI accepted only the expected BeeKemSafety dependency failure.

non_claims: No concrete signature, NIKE, or symmetric-encryption construction is proved secure by this manifest; named primitive-game probabilities remain the computational assumptions.
BeeKEM Appendix B and the internal algorithms of the existential witnesses BNike and BSe are imported paper evidence, not machine-checked EasyCrypt reduction bodies.
The theorem boundary's probability-one correctness premises are a narrower perfect-correctness specialization, not a proof of the paper's more general overwhelming-correctness case.
No arbitrary Byzantine behavior by a genuinely authorized BeeKEM member is covered.
No concrete Rust serialization, hashing, persistence, erasure, crash-recovery, zeroization, or operating-system residue property is proved here.
Live-key and ungranted-content-key confidentiality are separate unfinished application-level deliverables.

Page 10 prints a raw-success advantage definition inconsistent with Appendix B's neighboring-game differences; the imported theorem records and uses the uniform centered interpretation instead of concealing the discrepancy.

beekem_public_theorem.name: beekem_theorem1_imported_normalized
beekem_public_theorem.quantifier_shape: forall A, PaperInstance, memory, users, group, kappa, c, n, h, membership; side conditions imply exists BNike, exists BSe, bound
beekem_public_theorem.left_hand_side: centered bias of the exact executable BeeKemKiGame under challenger-computed bee_safe_kappa
beekem_public_theorem.right_hand_side: c * ceil(log2 n) times the sum of centered named HKR-CKS and MU-CPA advantages for existential Appendix-B reductions
